claim: The character card for 刺 leads with "Business card", which is the meaning of the word 名刺 it was generated for, not of the character, against card-rules-reading rule 9.
evidence: Card r-97cd3b2ec4e3: 刺 "Business card; stab", reviewNote "Not taught by the book yet: meaning and readings from KANJIDIC2"; characters.json review: "trimmed to two meanings led by the sense 名刺 uses". Book prints 刺 only in "名刺(めいし) name card", and this unit cards r-6106ca1d1492 名刺 "Name card". Rule 9: "A character's English is what the character itself means, never the meaning of a word it appears in."
fix: Change the English to the character's own sense, e.g. "Pierce; stab".
verdictReason: Card r-97cd3b2ec4e3 ships as 刺 "Business card; stab"; the book prints 刺 only inside 名刺, and 名刺 "Name card" (r-6106ca1d1492) ships in the same unit. One nuance: KANJIDIC2 does list "calling card" for 刺, so the gloss is not invented, but it is the dictionary's last sense after thorn, pierce, stab, prick, sting, and characters.json records the reviewer leading with "the sense 名刺 uses", which is exactly the pattern card-rules-reading rule 9 forbids (将 in 将来 is not "Future"). A silent kanji card is graded on meaning alone, so the lead sense is the whole card.
